harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1 (CentOS Stream 10, cronie), configured /etc/cron.allow to contain only root and opsadmin, restricting cron job scheduling to those two users. Created the opsadmin user since it did not previously exist. Verified via functional tests that root and opsadmin can install crontabs while other users are denied ("not allowed to use this program"). Performed the mandatory single-node restart of node1 (systemctl reboot), confirmed the boot_id changed (cce73776... -> 273bc930...), and re-verified post-restart that crond is active/enabled, /etc/cron.allow persisted, and the allow-list behavior still works correctly (opsadmin allowed, a fresh test user denied).
actions_performed: Inspected OS, existing users, and cron.allow/cron.deny state on node1
Created local user opsadmin (useradd -m)
Wrote /etc/cron.allow containing exactly 'root' and 'opsadmin', mode 644 root:root
Verified functionally: opsadmin and root can create crontabs; a disposable testuser is denied with cronie's standard rejection message
Cleaned up test crontabs and removed the disposable testuser
Captured healthy baseline: boot_id, crond active/enabled, cron.allow contents
Restarted node1 via 'systemctl reboot' (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned; confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart
Post-restart verified crond active/enabled, /etc/cron.allow persisted (root, opsadmin), and functional allow/deny behavior still correct against a fresh verifyuser
Cleaned up verifyuser and confirmed no leftover crontabs

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can schedule cron jobs (cron.allow configured)
evidence.summary: Confirmed no pre-existing cron.allow/opsadmin user, created opsadmin, wrote /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: allowed users succeed, others are denied
evidence.summary: sudo -u opsadmin crontab succeeded (rc=0) and installed a job; sudo -u testuser crontab was rejected with 'not allowed to use this program' (rc=1); root also succeeded
Removed test crontabs for opsadmin/root and deleted testuser after killing its lingering session
Captured boot_id cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64, crond active/enabled, and cron.allow contents (root, opsadmin) prior to restart
Backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' via nohup+disown; command returned 'reboot scheduled' immediately

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity (actual restart, not just downtime)
evidence.summary: Node became unreachable (connection timed out/reset) during reboot, then reconnected with a new boot_id 273bc930-4571-4fe4-9f28-c93141f9f8da, differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron access control and service health
evidence.summary: crond active/enabled after reboot, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root and opsadmin, opsadmin successfully scheduled a cron job while a fresh verifyuser was denied; cleanup confirmed
